episode_title: He Builds His Own Amazon Software (And Can't Code)

real_qa.q: How did Chad transition from working in the oil field to becoming a full-time Amazon FBA seller?
real_qa.r: Chad was laid off from an oil field water measurement company in 2020 when COVID-19 hit and oil prices crashed. He had been saving aggressively and possessed prior reselling knowledge from his grandfather's furniture flipping business. He initially flipped PS5s for cash while learning Amazon FBA through online communities, eventually transitioning full-time as that opportunity dried up. He committed fully to online arbitrage because he loved the data-driven nature of finding and playing sales cycles.
real_qa.requete: how Chad started Amazon FBA selling 2020

real_qa.q: What software tools has Chad built without coding experience, and how did he automate a state sales tax audit?
real_qa.r: Chad has built a RA scanning tool, various scrapers, his own version of a paid transcription app, and published a Keepa skill on GitHub despite not being able to write code. Most notably, he used Claude AI to knock out roughly 20 hours of work in 30 minutes for a state sales tax audit—saving approximately 100 hours of manual labor by pointing the AI tool at the clock and letting it process the data.
real_qa.requete: Chad AI tools built no coding experience

real_qa.q: Why did Chad avoid wholesale sourcing despite five years in Amazon selling?
real_qa.r: Chad has never found comparable margins with wholesale compared to online and retail arbitrage. He values the flexibility of arbitrage because he can scale up or down based on life changes without managing supplier relationships, which he believes requires constant nurturing to maintain access to the best deals. He prefers the arbitrage model because it keeps him on his own time rather than dependent on a wholesaler's inventory or terms.
real_qa.requete: why Chad does not use wholesale Amazon FBA

real_qa.q: How has Chad's sourcing split between online arbitrage and Amazon-to-Amazon flips changed over time?
real_qa.r: Approximately one and a half years ago, Chad was 70% online arbitrage and 30% Amazon-to-Amazon flips. Today, that split has shifted to roughly 50-50, depending on deal flow. During periods when Amazon matches prices on retail sites, he spends heavily on OA; during Q4, he focuses more on OA and RA. He emphasizes that he buys low and sells high regardless of the specific model, sometimes even purchasing from wholesalers if an arbitrage opportunity leads him to their distributors.
real_qa.requete: Chad sourcing split OA versus A2A flips ratio

real_qa.q: Why did Chad start selling used electronics on Amazon, and what initial success surprised him?
real_qa.r: Chad discovered the used electronics opportunity almost by accident when he found Nikon binoculars at Walmart for $50 that he initially couldn't list as new. After placing it on a shelf for three or four months, he decided to list it used and discovered the used offer was $180—only $20 under the new price—and it sold in a day. This experience made him realize he was sleeping on used inventory, and he has since built scrapers and feeds to identify refurbished and used deals, such as drawing tablets, where the margins make sense to sell as used.
real_qa.requete: Chad selling used electronics Amazon Nikon binoculars
